explanation: It was carved straight out of the limestone bedrock of the Giza plateau. More than 70 m (230 ft) long, it faces east toward the sunrise.

claims.text: The Great Sphinx of Giza has a human head on a lion's body.
The Great Sphinx does not have the body of a bull, a jackal or a falcon.
The Great Sphinx was carved directly from the limestone bedrock of the Giza plateau.
The Great Sphinx is more than 70 m long.

writerNotes: Self-check (§9.3). Lint: clean under content:check for writer w-part01w. Claims: every checkable statement in the stem, options and explanation is listed, with risk at or above the C26 floor and raised where a fact is beyond everyday knowledge. Datasets: no dataset covers the monument; c5 is a pure conversion (70 m is 229.7 ft) a calculation can confirm; c4 needs a source. Rival test: the bull, jackal and falcon are the animals of Apis, Anubis and Horus, real Egyptian confusions, but the Sphinx is a lion; against the key, nothing. Volatility: evergreen; no time words, and nothing depends on knowledge newer than mid-2026. Regional: known worldwide. Style: Oxford spelling, straight quotes, no en or em dashes, explanation within 35 words. Myths: screened against myths.json; I kept away from the nose story (napoleon-shot-sphinx-nose), so no hit. Mystery: not applicable to a practice item. Encore: not applicable to a practice item. Doubts: I left out the attribution of the face to Khafre, which most but not all Egyptologists accept (§1.7, disputed attributions stay out); c4 is bounded because published lengths vary around 73 m.
